primary_na: An agua-fresca-style drink of fruit, lime and a little salt: bright, acidic and lightly savory, served very cold.
alternate_na: A chilled, lightly sweetened tea with spiced citrus; tannin and citrus give a dry, refreshing edge without heat.
why_it_may_work: The beer is light and low in bitterness, so it should refresh against fried, medium-heat chicken without adding to the chile. The fruit-and-acid drink does the same job with lime and salt.
how_it_could_fail: A light lager could be too thin for the fat. A bitter pilsner or tannic tea could add to the chile burn. A sweet drink could feel heavy beside fried food.
deciding_test: Taste each drink beside the same chicken and chip at the start and after ten minutes, then ask whether the heat, fat and chip crunch feel better or worse.
na_safety_note: Fresh fruit drinks need review for unpasteurised juice, produce handling and holding time. Nothing here is a recipe; a food-safety professional must review shelf life, storage and service before any use.

primary_na: A spiced-citrus drink with a gentle herbal edge and light sparkle that echoes lime and cilantro.
alternate_na: A hop-water-style botanical drink, dry and aromatic, with citrus peel and no sweetness.
why_it_may_work: Citrus and herbal aroma should link to the cilantro, lime and char, and the acidity cuts the paneer's richness. The NA drinks aim at the same bridge.
how_it_could_fail: Coriander and citrus against the cilantro or lime could taste soapy to some guests. A strongly spiced drink could compete with the marinade.
deciding_test: Taste the beer and both NA drinks with the same taco, with and without cilantro, and note any soapy or clashing flavours.
na_safety_note: Botanical and hop-water-style drinks need review of ingredient sourcing, allergens and labelling. Nothing here is a recipe; a food-safety professional must review shelf life, storage and service before any use.

primary_na: A tea-based drink with tamarind or hibiscus acid and warm spice, served cool or slightly warm, matching the dish's chile and cinnamon notes.
alternate_na: A non-alcoholic beer with a malty, toasty, gentle-bodied character (a brewer or supplier to define; strength and labelling to be confirmed) to answer the braise.
why_it_may_work: Carbonation, acid and tannin cut the fat in the consomme, and warm spice in the drink can echo the adobo. The amber style bridges toasty malt to the braise.
how_it_could_fail: Clove and banana against the dish's clove and cinnamon is a gamble. A malty option could be heavy with a rich consomme. Too much sweetness would clog.
deciding_test: Taste the same goat portion with each option, alternating with the consomme, and note which one leaves the palate cleaner after a few bites.
na_safety_note: Tea, hibiscus and spice infusions need review of brewing, cooling and holding, and any warm service needs hot-holding checks. Nothing here is a recipe; a food-safety professional must review shelf life, storage and service before any use. A non-alcoholic beer is a brewing and labelling matter for a qualified brewer and an alcohol attorney; no strength claim is made.

primary_na: A lime-forward agua-fresca-style drink with a pinch of salt and a little green herb, cold and crisp.
alternate_na: A savory, saline drink with tamarind and a light spice, a nod to chaat flavours, kept thin and not sweet.
why_it_may_work: Crisp carbonation and light bitterness should reset the palate between bites of roasted, glazed cauliflower, and the lime and saline drinks echo the slaw and pickle.
how_it_could_fail: Bitterness beside chile heat could increase the burn, though the heat is modest here. The tamarind glaze plus a tamarind drink could be too sour or sweet.
deciding_test: Taste with the dish at the roast stage and again once the glaze has softened the crust, and compare each drink against the lighter Mexican-style lager.
na_safety_note: Saline and tamarind drinks need review of acidity, salt level, and holding time. Nothing here is a recipe; a food-safety professional must review shelf life, storage and service before any use.

primary_na: A lassi-inspired drink of cultured dairy, fruit and a little spice, served cold, to echo the sauce and cool the richness.
alternate_na: A spiced citrus tea with a sharp, dry finish to cut the cream and cheese.
why_it_may_work: Toasty malt bridges to the charred chicken, and a sharp or tart drink counters the cream, butter and cheese. A lassi-style drink echoes the sauce in a cooling way.
how_it_could_fail: Malt sweetness on a sweet cream sauce could cloy. A dairy drink beside a dairy-rich dish could feel heavy. Yeast spice could clash with the garam masala.
deciding_test: Taste each option beside the same wedge, and see whether the drink keeps the second bite as appealing as the first.
na_safety_note: Dairy-based drinks need particular review for pasteurisation, cold chain, shelf life and allergen labelling. Nothing here is a recipe; a food-safety professional must review shelf life, storage and service before any use.
